Solutions to the exercises in Chapter 2.

## Problem 1 {#sec-ch02-1}

A CDF is defined as $F_X(x) = \mathbb{P}(X \le x)$, meaning it is
right-continuous; $F(x) = F(x^+)$. Lemma 2.15 (proof in Problem 3) states
$\mathbb{P}(X = x) = F(x) - F(x^-)$. Therefore, $\mathbb{P}(X = x) = F(x^+) - F(x^-).$

## Problem 2 {#sec-ch02-2}

The given probabilities yield CDF:

$$
F(x) =
\begin{cases}
0   & x < 2, \\
0.1 & 2 \le x < 3, \\
0.2 & 3 \le x < 5, \\
1   & x \ge 5.
\end{cases}
$$

Therefore, $\mathbb{P}(2 < X \le 4.8) = 0.1$ and $\mathbb{P}(2 \le X \le 4.8) = 0.2$.

::: {.code-below}
```{python}
#| label: cdf-ch02-2
#| fig-cap: "Figure 2.2"
#| fig-alt: "Step function rising from 0 to 0.1 at x=2, to 0.2 at x=3, and to 1 at x=5, with filled dots at jump values and open dots at left limits."
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

segments = [(0, 2, 0.0), (2, 3, 0.1), (3, 5, 0.2), (5, 6, 1.0)]

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

for x0, x1, y in segments:
    ax.hlines(y, x0, x1, color="C0", lw=3, zorder=3)
    ax.plot(x0, y, "o", color="C0", markersize=7, zorder=4)
    if x1 < 6:
        ax.plot(x1, y, "o", markerfacecolor="white",
                markeredgecolor="C0", markersize=7, zorder=4)

ax.set_xlim(0, 6)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.5)
ax.set_xlabel("$x$")
ax.set_ylabel("$F(x)$")
ax.set_xticks(range(7))
ax.set_yticks([0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0])
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```
:::
